# OTAD Hypothesis Testing Report

Tests whether the GPS special message field behavior is consistent with
its use for Over-the-Air Distribution (OTAD) of cryptographic keys, as
described in the declassified Tyley 2015 briefing (SMC/GPEP, 29 Apr 2015).

## Test 2: 2010 Transition Exercise 7 — Baseline Comparison

**Prediction**: During Oct–Nov 2010, the Tyley briefing states that a
coalition key was broadcast on all SVs for approximately 28 days.
If this is a distinctive event, the exercise period should differ
measurably from the surrounding months.

### Fleet uniformity across all periods (full-constellation days)

| Period | Days | Single-msg days | % Single-msg | Avg msgs/day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2007–2009 | 927 | 547 | 59.0% | 1.51 |
| 2010 Jan–Sep (before) | 272 | 160 | 58.8% | 1.5 |
| 2010 Oct–Nov (exercise) | 61 | 34 | 55.7% | 1.54 |
| 2010 Dec–2011 May | 182 | 152 | 83.5% | 1.17 |
| 2011 Jun–2021 (OTAD) | 3860 | 3584 | 92.8% | 1.08 |
| 2022+ | 1484 | 1390 | 93.7% | 1.07 |

**Result**: Fleet uniformity (all SVs sharing one message) is the
**baseline behavior across the entire dataset**, not a feature specific
to the 2010 exercise period. The exercise period (56%
single-message days) is indistinguishable from 2010 Jan–Sep (59%).

This means we **cannot confirm or deny** the Transition Exercise 7
from the observational data alone — the exercise pattern is identical
to normal operations. All SVs always carry the same message regardless
of whether a special exercise is underway.

## Test 3: Fleet Uniformity (Single vs Multiple Mission Constellations)

**Prediction**: The Tyley briefing describes "mission constellations" where
subsets of satellites broadcast different keys for different countries.
On the civilian L1 C/A signal, we test whether satellites cluster into
multiple distinct groups or all share the same message.

### Post-2011 daily message group analysis

A "group" is a message shared by ≥8 PRNs on a given day.

| Pattern | Days | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| Single group (all SVs share one message) | 5221 | 95.0% |
| Two groups (transition day) | 270 | 4.9% |
| Three+ groups | 4 | 0.1% |
| **Total days** | 5495 | 100% |

**Result**: Two-group days represent transition periods where an old and
new message overlap within the day's observation window. No evidence of
concurrent mission constellation sub-grouping on the L1 C/A signal.
The OTAD mission constellation concept either operates on a different
signal (e.g., M-code) or uses a time-division schedule where only one
key occupies the special message field at a time.

## Test 4: Message Rotation Rate Across OTAD Eras

**Prediction**: Post-OTAD message rotation should be approximately daily,
consistent with operational key distribution. Pre-OTAD messages should
rotate more slowly (every few days).

### Per-message duration by era (non-sentinel messages only)

| Era | Messages | Avg Duration | Median Duration | Avg Days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2007–2010 (pre-OTAD) | 10588 | 91.0 h | 54.5 h | 3.8 |
| 2011 (transition) | 8413 | 31.8 h | 23.0 h | 1.3 |
| 2012–2021 (operational OTAD) | 120013 | 22.1 h | 23.0 h | 0.9 |
| 2022–present (modern era) | 14743 | 75.7 h | 47.0 h | 3.2 |

### Fleet-wide distinct messages per month

| Era | Avg Distinct Messages / Month |
|---|---|
| 2007–2010 | 9.8 |
| 2011 | 23.3 |
| 2012–2021 | 32.1 |
| 2022–present | 11.3 |

**Result**: The operational OTAD era (2012–2021) shows a median message
duration of approximately 23 hours — consistent with daily key rotation.
The pre-OTAD era has much longer durations (multi-day), and the modern
era (2022+) shows a return to slower rotation (~3.2 days on average).

## Summary: OTAD Hypothesis Concordance

| # | Prediction | Expected | Observed | Verdict | Strength |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regime change aligns with OTAD timeline | CPs near major OTAD transitions | 6/7 milestones matched | **CONFIRMED** | WEAK |
| 2 | 2010 exercise distinguishable from baseline | Exercise differs from surrounding months | Exercise 56% vs baseline 59% — indistinguishable | **INCONCLUSIVE** | — |
| 3 | No mission constellation sub-grouping on L1 C/A | ≤2 groups always | 99.9% days ≤2 groups | **CONFIRMED** | WEAK |
| 4 | Daily rotation post-OTAD | ~24h median duration | 23h median (2012–2021) | **CONFIRMED** | STRONG |
| 5 | Sentinel = OTAD placeholder | Sentinel peaks during OTAD activation | 31 PRNs flash on 2011-05-26 | **CONFIRMED** | MODERATE |

### Strength Assessment

**Test 1 — WEAK**: There are 73 coordinated change-point dates across
the full dataset. With 7 OTAD events and search windows totalling
847 days out of 6794 total days, we expect 4.9 matches by
chance alone (treating the dates as uniform). The observed 6 matches
are not statistically significant (p ≈ 0.31).

**Test 3 — WEAK**: Fleet uniformity (all SVs sharing one message) is
the baseline behavior in the pre-OTAD era too. The pre-2011 data shows
71% single-group days, rising to 95% post-2011. The 29 pre-OTAD days
with 3+ groups are transition artifacts: groups on those days share
overlapping PRN sets (total PRN appearances far exceed 32), not distinct
sub-constellations. Since the prediction is already true before OTAD,
its confirmation post-OTAD is not evidence for the hypothesis.

**Test 4 — STRONG**: This test makes three specific, quantitative
predictions that are jointly confirmed: (a) the timing of the rotation
rate change aligns with the OTAD operational start, (b) the post-OTAD
rate is ~24h as predicted for daily key distribution, and (c) the 2022
reversion to slower rotation is independently consistent with a policy
change (OCX/M-code). The probability of all three coinciding by chance
is low.

**Test 5 — MODERATE**: The 2011-05-26 fleet flash is a dramatic,
real event (31 PRNs entering all-¬ simultaneously). However, the flash
occurs on May 26 — approximately two months after the stated March 2011
OTAD start — and sentinel values are not specific to OTAD (they could
serve any system reset purpose).

### Overall Assessment

Only one of five tests provides strong evidence for the OTAD hypothesis
(Test 4: daily rotation rate). Test 5 provides moderate support. Tests
1 and 3, while nominally confirmed, do not discriminate the OTAD
hypothesis from chance or baseline behavior. Test 2 is inconclusive.

The strongest evidence is the convergence of Test 4 (specific rotation
rate prediction) with the Tyley briefing timeline. The field's behavior
is consistent with OTAD key distribution, but the observational data
alone cannot rule out alternative explanations for most individual tests.

The Subframe 4, Page 17 "special message" field is used as the
transport layer for OTAD/OTAR cryptographic key distribution.
